findings.evidence: Lines 51–53 quantify `t ≥ 0` but use `(Set.Ici t)`; the same set occurs at lines 60 and 76. The roadmap states the classical equation `u' = Au` on the half-line, whose interior derivative must include approaches from both sides.
findings.fix: Use `HasDerivWithinAt u ... (Set.Ici 0) t`, which is two-sided at positive times and right-sided only at the boundary; strengthen the orbit-derivative prerequisite/API accordingly. Update the identical characterization at line 60 and accessor at line 76.
findings.issue: `IsClassicalSolution` differentiates within `Set.Ici t`, so even at interior times it sees only future values. For `A = 0`, a right-continuous step function such as `u(t)=⌊t⌋` on nonnegative times satisfies this derivative equation while having jumps, hence is not a classical solution.

summary: The classical-solution predicate uses a right derivative at every time, making it substantially weaker than the abstract Cauchy problem and admitting discontinuous, nonunique solutions.
